Molecular vibrational spectra

The most widely spectroscopic techniques for molecular vibrational analysis are ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy, Infrared (IR) spectrocopy, and Raman spectroscopy, which used to provide information about transitions between electronic states of molecules, indirectly reflects the composition, structure, and bonding of a system.

Using optimized molecular strutures and subsequent frequency analysis, we can now obtain more detailed molecular vibration information. Accurate quantum chemical sofware and algorithm calculated frequencies can often guide the analysis of experimentally measured vibrational spectra. These theoritical vibrational spectroscopy studies play key roles in identification peaks of molecular species.

Now, we can calculate and simulate the UV, IR, and Raman spectra using Python packages and compare the results with experimental spectra data.

This page contains scripts for practical aspects of DFT and TD-DFT implementations to simulate vibrational spectra.
